errors.quote: A triple $T$ has indicator $t_T$ with $\langle t_S,t_T\rangle=|S∩T|-1$ ... and $\langle t_T,t_T\rangle=2$. So each line $\langle t_T\rangle$ is nondegenerate, and neighbors' lines are orthogonal.
errors.problem: This follows the definition of both forms in the same bracket notation, but the identity holds only for the bit form over Q. For the phase form (F_2^h, dot product), t_S·t_T=|S∩T| mod 2 and t_T·t_T=1 (paper lines 867-870). Read there, the page's formula gives <t_T,t_T>=2=0, so every triple line would be isotropic, and it makes complex neighbors (even intersection) non-orthogonal. The page's justification for the binary label case is therefore false.

errors.quote: A nonzero residual contains a coordinate unit vector, hence an orthonormal basis
errors.problem: Residuals involving the lines P or Q, such as P⊗t_X^⊥⊗Q, contain no coordinate unit vector of F^{⊗3}. P and Q are spanned by tensors of triple indicators of weight 3^{j-1} and 3^{3-j}. The paper instead tensors coordinate units of the factors with those generators to get a norm-one vector. It then uses nondegeneracy of the residual and the fact that nondegenerate nonalternating binary spaces have orthonormal bases.
The paper's H is normalized, (1/√2)[[1,1],[1,-1]]. With the usual ±1 Hadamard matrix, H diag(1,i)H=(1+i)I+(1-i)X=2C and H diag(1,-1)H=2X, so the stated identities are off by a factor 2.

errors.quote: Labels live in $\Phi=F^{\otimes3}$ ... Outgoing labels $A\otimes F$ on $X$ and $B'$ on $Y$ equal the next incoming ones
errors.problem: A⊗F, B' and P⊗F lie in F^{⊗j}, not in F^{⊗3}. The paper tensors every stage label by the line Q=<t_{a_{j+1}}⊗...⊗t_{a_3}> and says it suppresses Q. Without Q the asserted equality does not hold literally: the next incoming X label is A'⊗<t_{a_{j+1}}>⊗Q'.
